# Source-Bound Native Zero-MTP Reduction

This provisional F07 calculation, issue #12150 under #11791, creates a *new*
OpenSim artifact by replacing only the right and left locked metatarsophalangeal
(MTP) PinJoints with WeldJoints. The unchanged Rajagopal-Lai-Uhlrich source and
the scaled, club-bearing mixed-actuation factory are separate inputs. The latter
already changes scale, body properties, wrist/subtalar locks, grip and assistance;
passing the reduction does not validate those earlier construction decisions.

## Declared Source and State Domain

`native_mtp_reduction.py` requires the exact source XML SHA-256, an absent
output path, and the ordered target declarations
`((mtp_angle_r, 0 rad), (mtp_angle_l, 0 rad))`. It rejects any other target,
non-PinJoint or partial MTP replacement, source/default or achieved nonzero
value or speed, changed lock/clamp option, prescription, and a clamped zero
target on a range boundary. The actual Rajagopal MTP coordinates are clamped
but zero lies strictly within both native ranges. An XML dependency scan rejects
remaining references to either removed coordinate outside its joint; native
model initialization and inventory checks reject dangling components. The
operation never changes or writes the source. The output is serialized,
freshly loaded and compared; the receipt binds source/output/reducer hashes,
native version and loaded OpenSim extension hashes. The source XML hash covers
the entrypoint artifact, not a transitive visual-mesh/resource closure.

Both native models initialize using OpenSim's own `initSystem`, which may
assemble. Every surviving named continuous state value from the source's
achieved initialized state is then copied exactly to the reduced state. Two
further comparisons separately perturb the right ankle and pelvis-tilt
coordinates by 0.01 rad and their speeds by 0.02 rad/s, if both are unlocked
and the perturbation stays within the source range. Actual donor and factory
tests require all three samples. These samples do not establish equality over
a full trajectory, wrap-route changes or all 39 source coordinates.

## Mechanical Equivalence Calculation

For each common coordinate name, let a native unit-speed probe define one
column of $P_s$ in the source mobility ordering and $P_d$ in the derived
ordering. The derived map must have full row rank. The explicitly checked
source lift is $L=P_sP_d^+$, with $P_s=LP_d$ to numerical tolerance. Full native
mass matrices and total applied generalized force vectors at the *same* named
continuous state then obey the tested reductions

$$M_d=L^\mathsf{T}M_sL,\qquad f_d=L^\mathsf{T}f_s.$$

Here $f=J_{\mathrm{system}}^\mathsf{T}F_{\mathrm{body}}+f_{\mathrm{mobility}}$;
native body spatial forces include gravity and muscle forces. A synthetic
2 kg offset-mass PinJoint confirms that the mobility cache alone is zero
while the body-force projection is about $-19.6133$ N·m. The calculation does
not conflate total applied forces with inertial bias or constraint reactions.

The code also reports common-coordinate projections $P^\mathsf{T}MP$ and
$P^\mathsf{T}f$, body ground transforms and spatial velocities, muscle path
lengths, and native position/velocity constraint residuals. It requires
unchanged ordered body, muscle, actuator and constraint inventories and native
muscle properties. Errors are reported individually in each native quantity's
units; the fixture admission tolerance is $10^{-10}$ in those units. A sampled
mass/force and transform agreement is mechanical evidence, not an anatomy,
passive-force or transcription certificate. In particular the fixed MTP lock
reaction is not separately identified as a pin mobilizer reaction and cannot
be equated to the weld reaction without combining all source constraint loads.

## Executed Native Evidence and Limits

OpenSim `4.6-2026-06-22-85aaf64` passed eleven actual-native tests. A synthetic
nonzero locked PinJoint at 0.3 rad rejects before output, consistent with a
retained independent stock-operator counterexample showing 0.263874 transform
component error when that target is welded. An actuator referencing a removed
coordinate, changed source bytes, partial declaration, nonzero locked speed and
unlocked coordinate reject. The exact retained donor source SHA-256 is
`8708ed0d6a212080a72b9c277071ddd12939c8306efceb3ee4a9592735f43f80`.
Its 80 Millard muscles and 17 CoordinateActuators remain. The separately
serialized scaled/club factory uses golf-model SHA-256
`6b314c9607433d4a37129c1150ec7d5dc37ce74d1d8094c4f334983f5ab576f5`.
At the initialized, ankle-varied and pelvis-varied native poses, both freshly reloaded outputs
had zero reported body-transform, spatial-velocity, muscle-length, projected
mass/force, and full-lift mass/force differences; the scaled/club maximum
position/velocity constraint residual was $5.55\times10^{-16}$ in native units.
These values are source/runtime-specific diagnostic observations. The
repository turnover records exact commands and output hashes.

The original 80-muscle source still has six other locked joints, knee couplers,
no foot contact and no golfer-calibrated arm/trunk muscles. The derived factory
retains explicit upper/root/reserve torque assistance; it is not a pure-muscle
endpoint. Full-state numerical restart, time-varying native controls, active
wrap transitions, per-muscle force/power and active-wrap equivalence at multiple
constraint-consistent velocities, actual Moco feasibility and independent full-horizon excitation
replay remain separate gates. All 17 model variants and six engine families
remain in the epic denominator.
